newsitem.title: CANADA: Unions ask federal help for Canadian Air.
newsitem.headline: Unions ask federal help for Canadian Air.

text.p: The two biggest unions serving Canadian Airlines have asked the federal government to bail out the shaky carrier but on Wednesday met a muted response.

The biggest union, International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, asked Ottawa to give the airline C$70 million in assistance, noting the C$87 million interest-free loan Canada extended to Quebec-based Bombardier Inc.

That was under a Technology Partnership scheme for high-tech industries, however, and Industry Minister John Manley told reporters the union request did not fall under the Technology Partnership category.
"It's not a Technology Partnership request, I'm sure," he said.

The Canadian Auto Workers (CAW), the second biggest union in Canadian Airlines, asked the federal government to "play a key role in refinancing" Canadian and to reintroduce controls on pricing, routes and new entrants into the airline business.
Both unions made the request in a letter to Prime Minister Jean Chretien.
"I do not need to remind you of the economic and social importance of preserving these jobs," CAW President Buzz Hargrove wrote, noting that 16,500 jobs were at stake.
The unions had rejected a 10 percent cut in wages demanded by Canadian Airlines, saying they had already made major financial concessions.
But Canadian said on Wednesday it would not be requesting new federal assistance.
Spokeswoman Diana Ward said: "We don't think the government or any investor would be interested in funding losses and we need to prove that this is a viable plan.
"And the governments have both come out saying they're not going to bail us out. They've helped us by deferring principal payments to give us time."
Federal Transport Minister David Anderson has refused to speculate to reporters on whether federal funds would be available, arguing no request had been made.
But Alberta Premier Ralph Klein said his province would not be coughing up new funds.
The Canadian government, Alberta and British Columbia agreed to a one-month delay in repayments of capital from Canadian, officials said on Wednesday.
AMR Corp, parent of American Airlines, holds a minority stake in Canadian.
